method.scope: Named, sourced deals where AI is core to the company. This is a curated map, not a census: industry trackers count far more deals (see market context).

chains.title: Alphabet's AlphaFold bet keeps compounding

steps.label: Alphabet, GV & CapitalG join Thrive-led round
Isomorphic signs J&J
Abu Dhabi opens health data
DeepMind, Isomorphic & Meta fund Biohub's open cell data
Next round in talks: ~$5B at ~$50B (up from $2B+ at $40B+ in October)
Pharma answers with its own closed dataset: GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi join Cascade

chains.insight: Big tech money plus sovereign money (MGX, Temasek, UK Sovereign AI Fund) are funding the platform before it has clinical data, and the price keeps rising: the next round is now reportedly about $5B at roughly $50B. Pharma pays for access, Gulf states offer data, and Alphabet is also paying for shared biology data with an early-access window, while GSK, Pfizer and Sanofi joined a licensed rival dataset (Cascade), so the data race has an open and a closed track.

chains.title: Frontier AI labs buy into biology

steps.label: Anthropic buys Coefficient Bio
OpenAI re-invests in Chai

OpenAI-backed Chai adds Roche

OpenAI's fund leads Biossil's round
Biossil buys Theriva's shelved enzymes
Anthropic works on agentic CAR-T design with Generate Biomedicines
Ex-OpenAI executive Fidji Simo's ChronicleBio signs its first drug partner, Prolong

chains.insight: AI labs reach bio four ways: buying small teams, investing in model companies that sell to pharma, alumni who found companies, and owning drug programs outright (Anthropic–Mithril), now also via portfolio companies like Biossil that buy shelved clinical drugs. Anthropic's S-1 now pitches that bio push to public investors. Most terms stay undisclosed. Chai's Roche deal (Nov 5) makes seven pharma or biotech partners this year for one OpenAI-backed model company. Anthropic's collaboration with Generate, a public AI biotech, shows a lab working inside someone else's pipeline as well as building its own. Alumni companies are now earning pharma money too: ChronicleBio's Nov 12 Prolong deal is its first.

chains.insight: NVIDIA rarely leads a round, but it shows up in the cap tables of GPU-heavy companies, co-funds pharma's compute build-out, and now sits inside Danaher's lab instruments. With Iambic's IPO its portfolio is reaching public markets.

chains.title: Eli Lilly is investor, partner and customer at once

steps.label: Equity in Alchemab, NewLimit, Superluminal, BigHat and Fathom
Insilico licence
Profluent recombinases
METiS delivery deal
Fauna Bio names a second obesity target

chains.insight: Lilly shows up in more deals on this map than anyone else. It takes small equity stakes early (most recently Fathom's $55M physics-plus-AI Series A), signs licences with large milestone totals, and then pays them out step by step, as with Fauna Bio's second obesity target on Nov 11.

chains.insight: Some AI-first developers in-license assets from other biotechs (here Alphamab, a Chinese biotech), then raise from pharma to develop them. Investor cash goes to buying drugs as well as building models.

chains.title: States are buying a seat at the frontier

steps.label: UK Sovereign AI Fund in Isomorphic and Basecamp
UK Sovereign AI co-leads Potential Sciences' seed, plus supercomputer time
MGX & Temasek in Isomorphic
ADIA & IQT in Lila Sciences
British Business Bank leads Alchemab
Shanghai Pudong co-leads Drug Farm
Bpifrance's patient fund joins Orakl's Series A
Shanghai state tech investor leads Tourson's Pre-A

chains.insight: Sovereign and state funds mostly join late-stage rounds as co-investors and lead only small local deals, though the UK's Sovereign AI now co-leads seeds and pays partly in compute (Potential Sciences). The pattern looks like industrial policy, with each country backing its own champions. France's Bpifrance joined Orakl's Series A as a co-investor (Nov 12), fitting the same co-investor pattern. Shanghai's state tech investor leading Tourson Intelligence's Pre-A (Nov 9) is another local-lead case, two weeks after China Life Capital led BioGeometry's A+.

chains.title: AI money moves down the pipeline

steps.label: WhiteLab raises for AI-designed delivery
AstraZeneca joins Multiply Labs' robot manufacturing round
Lightspeed and Lux fund Warp's chemistry robots
Avego leads Opentrons' Series E for AI-run lab robots
BMS leads Pathos for AI-led trials
Boehringer and Microsoft test digital patient twins
Creandum seeds Atlas Bio's simulated Phase II trials
AstraZeneca and Oracle sign for AI trial recruitment
Formation Bio raises a fund to buy clinical-stage drugs
adsilico raises £10M for virtual-patient device trials
argenx buys Unnatural Products' ML-plus-parallel-synthesis peptide platform
Mitsui Chemicals backs iORGANBIO's AI-run cell and organoid lab
Unlearn models untreated outcomes for Structure's oral GLP-1 study
Norrsken and Singular back Orakl's organoid-based trial forecasting
Prolong funds a trial in ChronicleBio's AI-selected ME/CFS patients

chains.insight: In October, money moved past molecule design toward delivery, lab robots (Warp, Multiply Labs, Opentrons) and manufacturing, and now trial design, recruitment and clinical assets. Microsoft and Oracle are entering at the trial stage, and Formation Bio's $600M fund brings endowment and hospital money in to buy drugs that are already in the clinic. argenx's Nov 9 deal shows the exit route: a pharma partner that has seen the design-and-make loop work pays mostly in cash to own it. The loop now reaches the cells the drugs are tested on: Mitsui Chemicals' Nov 10 stake puts a materials supplier inside iORGANBIO's automated cell factory. On Nov 12 digital twins reached a mid-size obesity developer, Structure Therapeutics, through Unlearn. Europe's early-stage funds are joining at the trial stage too: Orakl's $34M (Nov 12) pays to predict cancer-trial outcomes from patient tumour organoids before pharma commits to a Phase 2. On Nov 12 the money reached patient selection itself: Prolong is paying ChronicleBio to pick which ME/CFS patients get an existing drug in a Phase 2a.
